findings.description: The filter stores Git's ignored-path output in a HashSet using OrdinalIgnoreCase on every platform. On a supported case-sensitive Linux worktree, an ignored marker directory and a distinct nonignored marker directory whose paths differ only by case are therefore treated as the same path. The nonignored directory is removed from the machinery list even though Git will include its files in the reviewed digest; it consequently remains in the materialized reviewer candidate and machinery-only changes can affect the certified source identity. Use path comparison semantics consistent with Git/filesystem case sensitivity (or preserve exact Git-returned path identity), and add a case-collision regression on a case-sensitive platform.
findings.title: Ignored-path matching collapses distinct paths on case-sensitive worktrees

summary: Risk-based review completed. Both controller-declared verification commands succeeded on the exact target digest. One cross-platform candidate-membership defect remains in the ignored machinery-path filter.
